page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is an ARM-based compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processors. The instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz on an arm64 architecture with single-threaded execution per core, eliminating hyperthreading contention. It is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. In addition to standard compute capacity, the instance includes 474 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluation shows balanced multi-core execution alongside modest single-thread throughput. Multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core (12,133.14) and Geekbench multi-core (5,364.0), fall into the average range across tested hardware, bolstered by software compilation scores reaching 8,140.0 in Clang. Conversely, single-threaded throughput reflects architectural limits, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 930.0 and weaker performance in compression tasks like bzip3 and gzip. Memory throughput is solid, delivering 116.89 GB/s for large-block uncached reads and 473.11 GB/s for cached operations.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the c6gd.2xlarge offers favorable compute density and operational throughput for parallelized arm64 workloads due to the efficiency of the Graviton2 silicon. Bundling 474 GB of local NVMe SSD storage provides immediate low-latency disk access without requiring separate block storage attachments. However, applications heavily reliant on x86 instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 or those requiring high single-thread clock speeds will experience performance tradeoffs.

Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is suited for multi-threaded workloads benefiting from direct local storage, such as distributed caching with Redis (achieving 9.43 million SET operations per second), static web serving, CI/CD code compilation pipelines, and containerized microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by 64-bit ARM AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processors. Configured with 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz and 16.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a compute-focused 1:2 core-to-memory ratio without hyperthreading overhead. A distinct physical attribute is its bundled 474 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by a 2 Gbps baseline network capacity. Benchmark results indicate steady multi-core execution, demonstrated by 12,133.14 in stress-ng multi-core and 9.43 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, counterbalanced by lower single-threaded metrics in Geekbench and compression routines. The instance offers strong resource efficiency for horizontally scaled, ARM-native services. Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge fits multi-threaded backend tasks, continuous integration build nodes, caching layers, and high-throughput static web serving.
